# Evidence: the LinkedIn channel

Ratings (this folder's scale, defined in `README.md`):

- **measured**: study or large dataset with a stated method, not run by a seller of the thing measured.
- **vendor, method stated** / **vendor, no method**: a seller's own data. LinkedIn counts as a vendor.
- **survey**: self-reported.
- **practice**: what experienced practitioners do; not measured.
- **untraced**: no source found, or the source does not say it.
- **platform rule**: LinkedIn Help describing its own product. Not evidence of an effect, a fact about the rules.

Everything is observational unless the row says randomized. Every source is in `sources.md`.

## Acceptance and reply benchmarks

| Claim | Source | Rating |
|---|---|---|
| A fictitious recent graduate requesting people LinkedIn recommended to them: about 23% to 26% accept; a shared employer or school about doubles it (almost 40%) | LinkedOut field experiment, about 20,000 US users, 400+ fictitious profiles, QJE 140(1), 2025 (absolute rates and the shared-tie figure from Zoe Cullen's NBER discussant slides, 2023) | measured (peer request, not a sales approach) |
| Acceptance 28.5%, message reply 10.4%, note reply 3.0% (3.5% to 2.2% over 12 months) | Expandi, 13,218,869 requests, 13,302 accounts, May 2025 to Apr 2026 | vendor, method stated |
| Acceptance median 20.75% (mean 23.85%); reply per accepted median 18.10%; weak below about 13% acceptance or 9.6% reply per accepted | HeyReach, 96,051 campaigns | vendor, method stated |
| 10.7% of campaigns with accepted connections got zero replies | HeyReach | vendor, method stated |
| Agency funnel: 18.7% accept, 17.6% of connected reply, 1.3% of connected book a meeting | Belkins, 14,077 contacts, 34 projects, 2025 | vendor, method stated |
| Connection median 1 day (62% within 24 h, 91% within 14 days); reply median 5 days; 60% of replies in week 1, 78.5% by day 14, 91.8% by day 30, 97.5% by day 60; meeting median 10 days | Belkins, 152,636 contacts, Mar 2025 to Feb 2026 | vendor, method stated |
| 21% of acceptances within 60 minutes, 63% in 24 h, 88% in a week, 99% in 30 days | Botdog, 16,492 requests (via Overloop and prior research) | vendor |
| Sender seniority moves acceptance within about 3 points (C-level 29.4%, junior 26.3%) | Expandi, 13.2M | vendor, method stated |
| Sender industry moves acceptance from 17.5% to 40.1% (both extremes on 14 to 16 accounts); staffing and recruiting top on acceptance among high-volume industries (36.5%), message reply 18.9% | Expandi, 13.2M | vendor, method stated (extremes small) |
| Reply by country: Netherlands 10.5%, US 6.0% | Belkins (Expandi 15M) | vendor |
| Campaigns under 30 days underperform (acceptance 13% first week, 27% at 180+ days) | HeyReach | vendor, correlational |

## Profile effects

| Claim | Source | Rating |
|---|---|---|
| Recipients read the face: same CV, different AI face, acceptance gap of about 3 points (13% relative) | LinkedOut, QJE 2025 | measured |
| Women senders: 36.2% acceptance vs 33.0% for men; reply 18.1% vs 15.6% | Waalaxy e-book 2025, about 20M invitations, 14.6M messages | vendor, sample stated, unadjusted |
| Non-Premium senders reply 17.2% vs 14.9% Premium | Waalaxy, 14.7M messages | vendor, sample stated |
| Senders with under 500 connections get more replies (about 18% to 19%) than 500+ (16%) | Waalaxy | vendor, sample stated |
| Recruiter senders get the most replies (25.6%), marketers the fewest (14.5%) | Waalaxy | vendor, sample stated |
| Accounts with 1,000+ followers and 3+ posts with 10+ likes: 30.5% acceptance vs 27% to 29% | Expandi H2, 38 accounts | vendor, small |
| Posting twice a week during a campaign: reply 29.5% to 36.0%, meetings 3.8% to 5.1% | Prospectio test 11, 5,550 prospects | vendor, randomized design claimed |
| Headline that says who you help: 29.58% vs sales title 25.81% | attributed to Expandi; not found on any Expandi page | untraced |
| A new headshot took one account from 11% to 34% | one consultant | untraced (single case) |
| Banner effect on acceptance | none found | none |
